{{Short description|Concept in trigonometry}}
In [[trigonometry]], the '''sinus totus''' (Latin for "total sine") was historically the radius of the base circle used to construct a [[sine]] table; that is, the maximum possible value of the sine.

Letting the notation <math>\operatorname{Sin} \theta</math> stand for the historical sine, and <math>\sin \theta</math> stand for the modern sine function,
:<math>\operatorname{Sin} \theta = R \sin \theta,</math>
where <math>R</math> is the ''sinus totus'', <math>R = \operatorname{Sin} 90^\circ.</math>
